analysis:
Examined the docs/reports/README.md index changes: the date bump and one new link (Qwen3.8-27B public tensor assistant). This is documentation only, with no threat-model-relevant behavior change; the other links are unchanged. The new link target 2026-11-05-qwen27-public-assistant.md is not in the supplied evidence, so its contents are unreviewed. The README describes it as parity evidence only, not a qualification claim.

Examined the GemmaCheck.swift patch. It is a benchmark and diagnostic CLI (darkbloom-cluster-tp-check), not the provider serving path. It adds an optional --layer-stride flag. The flag is validated as an integer in 0...64. It is rejected unless the path is paged and Gemma4TensorParallelModel.benchLayerStrideApplies(mode:) holds. The stride is added to the workload digest the ranks agree on before loading, so mismatched strides across ranks fail closed. The run body is wrapped in Gemma4TensorParallelModel.withLayerStride(layerStride). The patch also adds a timing note on stderr/log output. It contains only step-time statistics (p50 and min) and no prompt content, keys or tokens. The `generation` variable became an implicitly unwrapped optional. It is assigned in every branch inside the closure, or the closure throws. The `!generation.stepSeconds.isEmpty` read happens after the throwing call, so it cannot be reached unassigned.

Not visible: the implementations of withLayerStride and benchLayerStrideApplies, and whether withLayerStride mutates global or static state that a production serving path shares. The tool is a separate test executable with no attestation, coordinator, key or encrypted-transport interaction in the diff. I found no regression against TB-002, TB-007, TB-011 or A-001..A-020. The patch excerpt is truncated at the Report construction, so the remainder is unseen. Integration should confirm that withLayerStride scopes its override and restores the default, and that the product's default layer stride is not changed by this PR. That is outside the supplied evidence.
